chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of this variant
predictions: There will be no reproducible allele-specific TF occupancy or TF-dependent enhancer effect attributable to this C-to-T change in relevant breast cells.
The strong breast-cancer association may reflect a linked causal change, a non-TF mechanism, or another effect not mediated by this variant.
falsified_if: In relevant breast cells, the variant shows reproducible allele-specific binding by a TF and variant- or TF-perturbation demonstrates a corresponding allele-dependent regulatory effect.

chains.title: Hypothesized alt-enhanced FOXA1 binding affects a TOX3-linked enhancer

links.claim: FOXA1 occupies the variant-containing site in MCF-7; this chain hypothesizes stronger binding to alt T, but the supplied evidence has no allele-specific measurement or FOXA1 QBiC-SELEX result establishing that direction. FOXA1 is selected as a candidate because it is expressed and has MCF-7 occupancy at the site, not because it is shown to be the variant-sensitive factor.
The variant lies in distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3180851, with activity marks reported among ENCODE biosamples; these maxima do not establish activity in MCF-7 specifically.

TOX3 is a plausible target based on proximity and high breast-cancer L2G scores, but no supplied evidence directly links this cCRE to TOX3; the reported GTEx results do not provide a significant eQTL for the variant.

MCF-7 is a plausible context because FOXA1 is abundant there and ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant are reported in MCF-7; this does not establish MCF-7-specific activity of the cCRE or allele-specific binding.

This chain proposes that greater FOXA1 binding on T increases enhancer output and TOX3 expression, potentially contributing to breast-cancer risk. The variant is strongly associated with breast cancer and T is reported as the effect allele in several associations, but the regulatory chain and its effect on risk are untested; one listed association reports C as the effect allele.

predictions: If the binding hypothesis is correct, allele-informative MCF-7 FOXA1 ChIP-seq or CUT&RUN reads will be enriched for T over C at this site.
A variant-dependent FOXA1 or enhancer perturbation will change enhancer output and, if TOX3 is the target, TOX3 expression preferentially from the T-bearing haplotype.
falsified_if: Adequately powered allele-specific measurements show no FOXA1 enrichment on T, or show enrichment on C.
FOXA1 or enhancer perturbation produces no variant-dependent effect on enhancer output or on TOX3 expression.

chains.title: Hypothesized alt-enhanced GATA3 binding represses a TOX3-linked enhancer

links.claim: GATA3 occupies the variant-containing site in MCF-7; this chain hypothesizes stronger binding to alt T, but the supplied evidence has no allele-specific measurement or GATA3 QBiC-SELEX result establishing that direction. GATA3 is a candidate because it is highly expressed and has MCF-7 occupancy here, not because it is shown to be the variant-sensitive factor.
The variant lies in distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3180851, with activity marks reported among ENCODE biosamples; these maxima do not establish activity in MCF-7 specifically.

TOX3 is a plausible target based on proximity and high breast-cancer L2G scores, but no supplied evidence directly links this cCRE to TOX3; the reported GTEx results do not provide a significant eQTL for the variant.

MCF-7 is a plausible context because GATA3 is highly expressed there and ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant are reported in MCF-7; this does not establish MCF-7-specific activity of the cCRE or allele-specific binding.

This chain proposes that greater GATA3 binding on T represses enhancer output and lowers TOX3 expression, potentially contributing to breast-cancer risk. Neither repression nor the expression effect is established, and the risk association does not establish this mechanism; one listed association reports C as the effect allele.

predictions: If the binding hypothesis is correct, allele-informative MCF-7 GATA3 ChIP-seq or CUT&RUN reads will be enriched for T over C at this site.
Greater GATA3 activity or occupancy will reduce enhancer output and, if TOX3 is the target, reduce TOX3 expression preferentially from the T-bearing haplotype.
falsified_if: Adequately powered allele-specific measurements show no GATA3 enrichment on T, or show enrichment on C.
GATA3 or enhancer perturbation does not produce the predicted allele-dependent reduction in enhancer output or TOX3 expression.

args.query: chr16:52565276 TOX3 breast cancer variant enhancer functional study allele-specific

matrix.test: Reanalyze allele-informative MCF-7 FOXA1 ChIP-seq reads spanning the variant for allelic imbalance, accounting for mapping bias.

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible T-versus-C FOXA1 occupancy imbalance.
More FOXA1 reads from the T-bearing allele.
No required FOXA1 imbalance; GATA3, rather than FOXA1, is the proposed allele-sensitive factor.

matrix.test: Measure allele-specific GATA3 occupancy at the site in MCF-7 using allele-informative ChIP-seq or CUT&RUN reads.

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible T-versus-C GATA3 occupancy imbalance.
No required GATA3 imbalance; FOXA1 is the proposed allele-sensitive factor.
More GATA3 occupancy from the T-bearing allele.

matrix.test: Perturb the variant-containing cCRE in MCF-7 and measure allele-specific enhancer output and TOX3 expression.

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible variant-dependent TF-mediated change in enhancer output or TOX3 expression.
A FOXA1-dependent increase in enhancer output and TOX3 expression on the T-bearing haplotype.
A GATA3-dependent decrease in enhancer output and TOX3 expression on the T-bearing haplotype.

next_experiment: The cheapest discriminator between the top two hypotheses (H0 and H1) is allele-specific reanalysis of existing MCF-7 FOXA1 ChIP-seq reads spanning the variant, if the reads and genotype are informative. Test for T-allele enrichment while controlling mapping bias; no enrichment would favor H0 over H1, whereas reproducible T enrichment would support H1's binding prediction but would not by itself prove enhancer activity, TOX3 targeting, or disease mediation.
